label: GO after an unrewarded trial, when the agent is choosing a1
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never at D1 or D2), and almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (98% of activation mass has prev_reward == 0; it never fires when the reward input is 1). Within those steps it is strongly biased toward the agent choosing a1: model_act == 1 holds 86% of the mass, and the activation rises with the a1-minus-a2 policy logit (rate 19% in the top choice bin, 0 in the bottom bin). The predicate uses the agent own GO choice (model_act), which the agent computes at that step, so it uses no future variable; action == 1 gives nearly the same score. GO & prev_reward == 0 alone has mass recall 0.98 but precision 0.26. Rate also climbs over the episode (0.7% in trials 0-9 to about 6% in trials 60-89), and requiring ep_trial >= 30 lifts dev F1 only from 0.58 to 0.60, so it was left out. Precision stays incomplete: many unrewarded a1-choice GO steps are inactive, and some activations come on unrewarded GO steps where the agent picks a2. The weakest activations are the ones that fall outside the predicate. Dev: P 0.49, R 0.71, F1 0.58, mass recall 0.85.
